data.content_ref: inline:The target answers the 'single mechanism best explains why the gap is larger in some cities' question with anthropogenic heat flux, but this is empirically the weaker cross-city predictor. The dominant, widely-cited cross-city modulator of nocturnal UHI intensity is urban geometry / sky-view factor (street-canyon effect): reduced view of the cold sky retards longwave radiative loss, so denser, taller urban fabrics keep a larger nocturnal gap. The target mentions sky view only as a passing token (the commitment list) while elevating anthropogenic heat, even though its own countercondition admits the mechanism is insufficient if reducing emissions does not shrink the gap — which is the established finding that geometry dominates. Thus it misidentifies the single best mechanism.
